hero.headline: FBI seizes computers in search of Ohio voter registration group offices
hero.body:
Federal agents conducted a raid on the Cleveland office of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative, a grassroots organization focused on voter registration, prompting concerns about potential enforcement actions against voting rights groups ahead of the midterm elections.

According to Prentiss Haney, a board member of the group, FBI agents seized computers and phones during Thursday's operation. Agents also visited homes of people affiliated with the organization throughout Ohio and conducted interviews with them.

The investigation appears to focus on accusations related to the 2024 election, though specific details remain unclear. The FBI's Cleveland office did not respond to requests for comment about the raid or its underlying investigation.

Haney characterized the operation as part of a broader campaign. "This raid is a full-on coordinated assault weaponizing the justice department and DHS against people who are fighting for working-class voters and Black voters to make sure they have access to the ballot," he said.

The timing of the raid came approximately one month after Todd Blanche, a top official in the acting attorney general's office, instructed prosecutors to prioritize voter fraud cases. Additionally, Frank LaRose, Ohio's Republican secretary of state, referred over 1,000 individuals he identified as non-citizens who appeared to have registered in the state to the justice department last fall. Federal investigators have also gathered voter records from at least six Ohio counties.

The operation drew immediate criticism from Democratic elected officials and civil rights organizations. Shontel Brown, an Ohio congressional representative whose district includes Cleveland, called it "an unprecedented attack on democracy" and stated the raids must end. She characterized the action as part of a systematic effort to attack elections and promote voter fraud myths.

Sherrod Brown, a former senator now running for office, described reports of the raid as "deeply disturbing." Cleveland Mayor Justin Bibb called for transparency, saying the FBI should disclose the basis for its actions or face questions about whether it was unfairly targeting civic participation.

Michael Waldman, president of the Brennan Center for Justice, described the raid as "an outrageous fishing expedition" designed to intimidate people working for democratic participation. He characterized it as an abuse of law enforcement for political purposes that fits a pattern of federal inquiries targeting voting infrastructure before elections.

Ohio remains a significant swing state in national elections. The state delivered 17 electoral votes to Donald Trump in 2024, and Republican Bernie Moreno defeated longtime Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown in a competitive race that helped Republicans gain control of the Senate.

Trump has repeatedly claimed widespread voter fraud without providing evidence, most recently focusing on California's vote-counting procedures.

cards.headline: US and Iran say cease-fire deal close as Hormuz reopening expected
cards.body:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran "has been largely negotiated," following conversations with Pakistani mediators, Gulf allies, and Israeli leadership. Trump stated on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" were still under discussion but would be announced shortly. He confirmed that reopening the Strait of Hormuz would be part of the agreement.

"An agreement has been largely negotiated, subject to finalization between the United States of America, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and the various other Countries," Trump posted.

However, Iran's response created immediate uncertainty. Iran's Fars news agency, which has close ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, disputed Trump's characterization. The agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran." It also said Trump's assertion that an agreement was nearly final was "inconsistent with reality."

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif later praised Trump's peace efforts and indicated that Pakistan hoped to host another round of talks between the US and Iran soon. Sharif described Trump's calls with leaders from Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Pakistan as "very useful and productive." Pakistan's army chief, Syed Asim Munir, has played a key role in the negotiations, meeting recently with Iranian officials including President Masoud Pezeshkian.

According to reports, Iran and Pakistan submitted a revised proposal to the United States. The draft agreement reportedly includes provisions for the strait to reopen with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, with Iran permitted to freely sell oil and negotiations on its nuclear program. In exchange, the US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports. Regional sources indicated the deal would include an official declaration ending the war, two months of negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, and potential release of approximately 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets.

Trump said he had spoken with leaders of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, and Bahrain, as well as Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's president. He also mentioned calls with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The announcement came after Secretary of State Marco Rubio hinted during a visit to India that news might arrive soon. However, Trump's earlier comments had suggested a deal could be signed this weekend, creating confusion when Iranian officials contradicted those claims.

The potential agreement has faced criticism from Republican hawks, with former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo denouncing the rumored terms as too favorable to Iran.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement on nuclear deal, senior official says
cards.teaser: The United States is close to finalizing an agreement with Iran, with a senior US official estimating an 80 to 85 percent chance of success in the near term.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he is canceling planned missile strikes on Iran, saying a peace deal is near. A senior US official estimates an 80 to 85 percent chance of success for a near-term agreement, though nuclear details will take months to finalize.

Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday that he expected to sign a deal with Iran within days. However, Iran's foreign ministry has not confirmed that a final decision on an agreement has been reached, dismissing Trump's claims about the timeline.

cards.headline: European Union agrees to begin membership talks with Ukraine and Moldova
cards.teaser: EU envoys approved launching the first phase of accession negotiations with both countries.
cards.body:
The European Union agreed to launch the accession process for Ukraine and Moldova, with envoys greenlighting the first phase of membership talks. President Costa and President von der Leyen issued a joint statement confirming the agreement to open the first accession negotiations cluster with both countries.

The decision marks a significant step forward for Ukraine and Moldova in their efforts to join the bloc. The move will allow both countries to begin formal negotiations on aligning their laws and institutions with EU standards, though the full membership process typically takes years to complete.

cards.headline: SpaceX completes IPO at $135 per share, closes up 19% on first trading day
cards.body:
SpaceX made its long-anticipated debut on public markets Friday, closing at $160.95 per share, a 19% jump from its $135 IPO price. The aerospace and artificial intelligence company completed the largest initial public offering in history, raising approximately $75 billion and achieving a market valuation of $2.1 trillion by day's end.

The strong first-day performance reflected robust investor demand. Shares opened around $150 and climbed significantly during the trading session, reaching highs near $176 before settling slightly lower in the final two hours. The successful debut marks a major milestone for the company, which operated as a private venture for nearly two and a half decades.

"It is certainly hard to believe that a little company that started in a warehouse in El Segundo is now going public with the largest IPO ever," Elon Musk said during an address at SpaceX's headquarters Friday morning. Musk reiterated the company's mission to "make humanity multiplanetary" and "take the fiction out of science fiction."

The IPO's success elevated Musk to an unprecedented status as the world's first trillionaire, according to reports. His fortune has grown dramatically over the past decade, increasing from approximately $14 billion ten years ago to its current astronomical level.

The offering attracted significant attention from institutional and retail investors alike. The Nasdaq exchange fast-tracked SpaceX's inclusion in its index, guaranteeing additional buying pressure from tracker funds and other index-following investments. This means many Americans with 401(k) retirement accounts and mutual funds now hold stakes in the company, according to Gallup data showing 62% of American adults invested in the stock market.

The public debut generated political and social backlash regarding wealth inequality. Democratic senators including Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren criticized Musk's extreme wealth accumulation, calling for legislation to tax ultra-wealthy individuals. "The typical American household would have to work more than 11 million years to make Elon Musk's level of wealth," Warren posted. "We need a wealth tax."

California Governor Gavin Newsom and other Democratic officials also weighed in, with Newsom stating "when the federal government is for sale, the rich get richer and everyone else gets shafted." Anti-billionaire protesters gathered outside JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters, warning that the IPO would "pilfer the retirement funds of working people."

Economist Gabriel Zucman warned that economic disparities highlighted by Musk's wealth accumulation could have profound societal effects. "The battle between democracy and oligarchy will be the defining battle of the 21st century," Zucman said.

As a publicly traded company, SpaceX now faces increased scrutiny and new disclosure requirements. The company's filings revealed it loses billions of dollars annually while primarily generating profits through its satellite internet service.

cards.headline: Justice Department Approves Paramount Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery
cards.teaser: The $111 billion merger would unite two major studios and place CNN and CBS News under the same corporate ownership.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has approved the $111 billion merger of Paramount and Skydance to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, removing a major regulatory obstacle for the deal. The antitrust division completed its review after months of scrutiny.

The merger would combine two major film studios and integrate their news operations, bringing CNN under the same corporate umbrella as CBS News. The deal faces continued scrutiny in the UK and could encounter legal challenges from state attorneys general.

cards.headline: Trump administration moves to limit Census Bureau data releases
cards.teaser: New policies could reduce public access to redistricting data and other statistics as officials restrict privacy protection methods.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is pushing to reduce privacy protections used by the Census Bureau when releasing public statistics, potentially decreasing available data for redistricting and research purposes. Officials are targeting what they call "statistical noise"—the techniques the Census Bureau employs to prevent identification of individuals in published data.

The Census Bureau currently uses various methods to balance privacy protection with data utility for users including state legislators, researchers, and the public. Redistricting data derived from the decennial census is essential for states to draw congressional and legislative district boundaries.

cards.headline: US deports Iranian pro-democracy activist to Central African Republic
cards.teaser: An Iranian woman who fled her country was among migrants deported under a new agreement.
cards.body:
The United States deported an Iranian pro-democracy activist to the Central African Republic as part of a new deportation agreement, according to lawyers representing the woman. Multiple Iranian women who fled Iran are being sent to the central African nation under the arrangement.

The deportations represent a shift in US policy regarding Iranian nationals seeking asylum. Lawyers and advocacy groups have raised concerns about sending deportees to the Central African Republic, a country that has experienced significant violence and instability in recent years.

cards.headline: Switzerland to vote on capping population at 10 million
cards.teaser: Swiss voters will decide on what would be the world's first national population cap.
cards.body:
Switzerland will hold a referendum on a proposal to cap the country's population at 10 million people. The right-wing Swiss People's Party frames the plan as a "sustainability initiative," though opponents characterize it as problematic and potentially chaotic.

The vote represents an unprecedented attempt to impose a national population limit through democratic means. The proposal has sparked debate between supporters who argue it will manage growth and preserve quality of life, and critics who warn it could damage the economy and Switzerland's standing as a global business center.

cards.headline: Afghans hold rare protests against Taliban as two killed
cards.teaser: Demonstrations erupted in support of arrested women, with the UN reporting casualties and dozens detained.
cards.body:
Afghans staged uncommon public demonstrations against Taliban policies, with two people killed during the protests. The demonstrations were organized to support women who had been detained by the Taliban regime.

The United Nations expressed deep concern over the arrests of dozens of women in recent days. Public protests against Taliban rule have been rare since the group returned to power, making these demonstrations particularly significant.

cards.headline: Pope Leo returns to Vatican on Spanish king's jet after mechanical issue
cards.teaser: The papal plane experienced a technical problem, forcing Pope Leo to borrow aircraft from King Felipe.
cards.body:
Pope Leo returned to the Vatican on an aircraft provided by Spain's King Felipe after his papal plane experienced a mechanical issue. The pope's flight home from Spain was delayed when the aircraft was grounded, forcing him to remain in the country while repairs were arranged.

The Spanish king offered his jet to transport the pontiff back to Rome. Pope Leo had completed a visit to Spain on Friday, where Catholic leaders discussed prospects for spiritual renewal in an increasingly secular nation.

cards.headline: World Cup opener in Mexico City held amid teacher protests over pay
cards.teaser: Groups including teachers unions demonstrated about wages and pensions during the tournament's opening game.
cards.body:
Mexico City's World Cup opening match took place as teacher unions and other groups continued demonstrations over pay and pension disputes. The protests, which had been ongoing for weeks, coincided with the tournament's launch.

Ticket prices for the opening game were steep enough to be unaffordable for most local fans. The BBC gained access inside the renovated Azteca Stadium ahead of the inaugural match.

cards.headline: Justice Department approves Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery
cards.teaser: Federal regulators cleared a proposed $110 billion merger between two major entertainment companies.
cards.body:
The Justice Department closed its investigation into the proposed merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, concluding the combination would not harm competition or consumers. The decision clears a major regulatory hurdle for the $110 billion to $111 billion transaction uniting two rival studio operations.

The merger would combine Paramount, which owns CBS, with the larger Warner Bros. Discovery, whose properties include HBO and CNN. The combined entity would create one of the largest entertainment conglomerates in the United States, consolidating significant television, film, and streaming assets under single ownership.

cards.headline: Elon Musk becomes first person to reach trillion-dollar net worth
cards.teaser: The tech entrepreneur's wealth hit $1.11 trillion as SpaceX went public with a $2.2 trillion market valuation.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire, with his net worth reaching $1.11 trillion according to Bloomberg's wealth tracking list. The milestone was driven by SpaceX's listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange, which valued the space exploration company at $2.2 trillion.

Musk, who leads X, Tesla, and SpaceX, has already held the title of world's richest person. His fortune has grown substantially as his various companies have expanded their market presence and valuations over recent years.

cards.headline: US and Iran signal peace agreement near completion
cards.teaser: Officials from multiple countries say negotiators have reached final text of a deal to end hostilities.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he is canceling planned strikes on Iran and claimed the two nations are on the verge of signing a peace agreement. This follows two days of escalating attacks that threatened to destabilize the ceasefire between the countries.

However, Iran's foreign ministry disputed Trump's characterization, stating that no final decision on an agreement has been reached. The conflicting statements highlight the fragile state of ongoing negotiations between the US and Iran.

cards.headline: US fans gather ahead of World Cup match against Paraguay
cards.teaser: Supporters assembled at the FIFA Fan Festival in Los Angeles before the national team's game.
cards.body:
American soccer fans gathered at the FIFA Fan Festival in Los Angeles to show their support ahead of the US national team's World Cup match against Paraguay. The atmosphere was enthusiastic, with supporters expressing their anticipation for the game.

The 2026 World Cup is being hosted across North America, with matches taking place in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. This marks a significant moment for soccer in the US, bringing the world's largest sporting event to North American soil.

cards.body:

The plan has drawn criticism from opponents who argue it would be chaotic and unworkable. Swiss voters will decide whether to adopt the population limit, which would significantly impact the country's immigration and demographic policies.

hero.headline: Index Fund Holders to Gain SpaceX Exposure Through Automatic Inclusion
hero.teaser: Retirement accounts and index funds will soon hold SpaceX shares as the company joins major market benchmarks.
hero.body:
Millions of Americans invested in index funds and 401(k) retirement accounts will automatically gain ownership stakes in SpaceX following the company's historic initial public offering, one of the largest stock market debuts ever.

SpaceX went public on Friday with an opening share price of $150, which quickly climbed higher during trading. The company's valuation exceeded $2 trillion by market close, making it a significant addition to major stock indexes. As SpaceX becomes included in these indexes, passive investors holding broad market funds will instantly own portions of the aerospace company without taking any action.

The automatic inclusion represents a major shift in SpaceX ownership. Previously, stakes in the company were limited to private investors and employees. Now, ownership has broadened dramatically to encompass millions of ordinary Americans saving for retirement through standard investment vehicles.

"It is certainly hard to believe that a little company that started in a warehouse in El Segundo is now going public with the largest IPO ever," Elon Musk said during remarks at SpaceX's headquarters on Friday morning. He emphasized the company's mission to "make humanity multiplanetary" and noted the company's journey from its early days.

The IPO made Musk the world's first trillionaire based on his ownership stake in the company. Financial analysts are currently calculating how much SpaceX stock will appear in typical retirement portfolios based on the company's market capitalization and how heavily it will be weighted within major indexes.

The inclusion of SpaceX in index funds comes as the broader stock market continues climbing. The S&P 500 recently crossed 7,000 for the first time, driven partly by technology sector strength and investor optimism around artificial intelligence. SpaceX, which operates both as an aerospace company and an artificial intelligence company, fits squarely within this trend.

Some observers have raised concerns about the implications of SpaceX's automatic inclusion in retirement accounts. A Guardian analysis noted that Americans are increasingly worried about artificial intelligence's future impact, with eight in ten expressing concern according to recent polling. The automatic investment means skeptical Americans will now have their retirement savings tied to the technology sector's continued growth, whether they actively support these developments or not.

SpaceX's valuation at IPO reflected massive confidence in the company's long-term prospects, despite the aerospace industry's inherent risks and challenges. The company's shift from private to public ownership marks a turning point for the space sector and signals major investors' belief in commercial space activities as a significant economic force.

The timing of the offering, which occurred in mid-June, aligned with symbolic dates according to reporting on the company's planning process, though the fundamental driver remained investor demand and market conditions.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Becomes First Person to Reach $1 Trillion Net Worth
cards.teaser: Musk's personal wealth crossed the trillion-dollar threshold as SpaceX shares soared in their trading debut.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire, with his net worth reaching $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list. The milestone followed SpaceX's initial public offering on the Nasdaq, where the company was valued at $2.2 trillion and its stock surged 20 percent on the first day of trading.

Musk's wealth has been built primarily through his ownership stakes in SpaceX and Tesla. When he founded SpaceX in 2002, he gave the aerospace company less than a 10 percent chance of success—a far cry from its current status as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise on Reports of Iran Nuclear Deal Progress
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed higher Friday amid optimism about diplomatic negotiations with Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump announced on Thursday that he was canceling planned missile strikes on Iran, stating that the two countries were on the verge of signing a peace agreement. The announcement came after two days of escalating attacks that had threatened a fragile ceasefire between the U.S., Israel, and Iran.

The diplomatic developments boosted investor sentiment, lifting major stock indexes Friday. The positive market reaction was further fueled by SpaceX's successful market debut, with shares surging 19 percent on the Nasdaq. The combination of easing geopolitical tensions and the strong IPO performance helped drive broader gains across multiple sectors.

cards.headline: SpaceX Shares Surge 20% in Record-Breaking Stock Market Debut
cards.teaser: SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Friday, with shares climbing 20 percent by market close in what became the largest initial public offering in .
cards.body:
SpaceX made its public debut on the Nasdaq under ticker SPCX, with shares closing up 20 percent on its first day of trading. The company's $2.2 trillion valuation marks the largest initial public offering in history. The successful listing signals a major shift for the private space industry, with OpenAI and Anthropic expected to pursue similar public offerings.

The IPO's success extended beyond Wall Street—trading platform Robinhood experienced record traffic as investors rushed to buy shares. Elon Musk, SpaceX's founder, saw his net worth reach $1.11 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire according to the Bloomberg rich list. SpaceX's entry into public markets gives retail investors and index fund holders access to one of aerospace's most prominent companies.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Paves Way for OpenAI and Anthropic Public Offerings
cards.teaser: The successful debut is expected to encourage other major private technology companies to pursue stock market listings.
cards.body:
SpaceX completed the largest initial public offering in history, with shares rising 20 percent on their debut. The successful offering has energized the IPO market and signaled strong investor appetite for major technology companies seeking public listings.

The strong market reception to SpaceX's debut is paving the way for other prominent firms to go public. OpenAI and Anthropic, two leading artificial intelligence companies, are among those expected to pursue stock market listings in the near term. Together with companies like Meta, Nvidia, and Google, these offerings represent a shift in which technology firms are driving major IPO activity.

cards.headline: Blake Lively Awarded Legal Fees Following Settlement with Justin Baldoni
cards.teaser: A court ruled Lively will receive payment for legal costs related to part of her dispute with her former co-star.
cards.body:
Blake Lively was awarded legal fees Friday in a court ruling that followed her settlement with Justin Baldoni. The decision covers costs associated with a portion of her legal battle with Baldoni, with whom she appeared in a film. The specific amount of the fee award has not yet been determined.

The ruling represents a partial resolution in the dispute between the two actors. The court's decision to grant legal fees indicates Lively prevailed on at least some aspects of the case, though the award only addresses expenses from part of the broader court proceedings.

cards.headline: Critical vulnerability found in Oracle PeopleSoft software
cards.teaser: A zero-day vulnerability in PeopleSoft software affects hundreds of organizations and allows data theft.
cards.body:
A vulnerability in Oracle-owned PeopleSoft software has been discovered that affects hundreds of organizations. The security flaw allows attackers to steal gigabytes of data from affected systems.

Security researchers describe the vulnerability as critical in severity. The zero-day designation indicates the flaw was unknown to the vendor before being exploited or discovered. Organizations using PeopleSoft for enterprise resource planning and human resources management face exposure until patches become available.

cards.headline: Google sues Chinese cybercrime group for AI-powered text message scams
cards.teaser: The tech company filed suit against a group that used artificial intelligence to defraud hundreds of thousands of victims.
cards.body:
Google has sued a Chinese cybercrime group called Outsider Enterprise for running AI-powered text message scams. The operation targeted hundreds of thousands of victims, sending 2.5 million fraudulent messages over just two weeks.

The group used artificial intelligence to generate and distribute the deceptive messages at scale. Google's lawsuit aims to disrupt the scam operation and hold those responsible accountable for the widespread fraud campaign.

cards.headline: FISA surveillance authority expires while spying continues under existing certifications
cards.teaser: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act expired, but surveillance activities will continue into 2027.
cards.body:
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act expired, but ongoing surveillance operations will continue under existing certifications. The law authorized warrantless surveillance of foreign targets, but existing certifications remain valid until March 2027.

The expiration does not immediately halt intelligence collection activities conducted under the law. The certification system allows surveillance programs to continue operating even after the authorizing statute lapses. Congress has debated reauthorization of Section 702, with privacy advocates and intelligence agencies presenting conflicting positions on the program's scope and oversight.

cards.headline: Jeff Bezos launches Prometheus startup focused on physical AI applications
cards.teaser: The new company joins other well-funded ventures working on artificial intelligence for physical systems.
cards.body:
Jeff Bezos has launched Prometheus, a startup developing physical AI technology aimed at creating an "artificial general engineer" for the physical world. The company focuses on AI-powered engineering tools to automate design processes for physical products and applications like drug design.

Prometheus has raised $12 billion in funding and is valued at $41 billion, positioning it as one of the best-capitalized companies in the physical AI sector. The startup competes in a growing field of well-funded competitors working on similar technologies that enable AI systems to interact with and control physical devices and robots.

cards.headline: Mistral AI reportedly raising $3 billion at $23 billion valuation
cards.teaser: The French AI company is in talks for funding that would double its previous valuation.
cards.body:
Mistral AI is raising €3 billion in a funding round that values the company at €20 billion (approximately $23.15 billion), according to reports. This valuation nearly doubles the French AI startup's Series C valuation of €11.7 billion.

The funding would establish Mistral as one of Europe's most valuable AI companies. The startup develops large language models and AI tools for both enterprise and consumer markets.

cards.headline: Ukraine conducted test using fully autonomous drones in combat
cards.teaser: The military tested drones that independently selected and engaged targets without human approval.
cards.body:
Ukraine conducted a test using fully autonomous drones that killed Russian soldiers without human intervention in targeting decisions. The one-time test represents a rare use of complete autonomy in lethal military operations.

Ukraine has been installing AI modules on drones and robotic systems throughout the conflict. Full autonomy, where machines select and engage targets without human approval, remains uncommon in military operations. The test indicates advancing capabilities in autonomous weapons systems, though Ukraine continues to primarily use human-controlled or semi-autonomous platforms for most operations.

hero.headline: Wyatt-Hodge scores century as England thrashes Sri Lanka in T20 World Cup opener
hero.body:
Danni Wyatt-Hodge hit an unbeaten 105 to guide England to an 87-run victory over Sri Lanka in the Women's T20 World Cup opener at Edgbaston on Friday evening. The triumph represented a dominant display from the hosts, who set a tournament record with their batting performance.

England accumulated 219 for the loss of just one wicket, the highest total in Women's T20 World Cup history. Sri Lanka's reply fell well short, reaching only 132 all out as they struggled against English bowling and fielding.

Wyatt-Hodge and Amy Jones, who opened the innings together, established a powerful foundation with a 135-run partnership. Jones eventually fell in the 14th over attempting to clear the infield, caught by Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. Nat Sciver-Brunt then took over, striking an unbeaten 46 from just 22 balls with apparent ease.

The match came down to a tense finale as Sciver-Brunt dominated the final over, hitting back-to-back boundaries. This left Wyatt-Hodge stranded on 97 with few opportunities to reach three figures. Sri Lanka's fielding came to England's aid when they cut off Sciver-Brunt's boundary attempt, allowing Wyatt-Hodge back on strike. She swept the next delivery into the gap behind square for four runs to bring up her century with a single ball remaining.

Wyatt-Hodge's celebration proved particularly poignant. Having given birth to her daughter Daisy just three weeks earlier, she cradled her bat like a baby in tribute to the crowd's applause. "I've been after that third T20 hundred for a few years now, so I'm chuffed to bits to get it," she said afterward. "I've had a big life change the last few weeks, so it was pretty emotional. A few of the girls said they had a few tears."

Later in the match, Wyatt-Hodge took a crucial catch racing back from square leg to dismiss Athapaththu, though she admitted the windy conditions made the catch difficult. "I thought I was going to run into the umpire," she explained. "It was really windy and blustery. I lost the ball for a couple of seconds and then managed to see it, put my hands out and grabbed it."

Sri Lanka's innings never gained momentum after losing their captain. The side slipped to 67 for five as batters attempted aggressive strokes without success. Freya Kemp proved particularly effective with the ball, taking a career-best four for 22 through consistent line-and-length bowling.

Sri Lanka's coach Jamie Siddons acknowledged his team's poor execution. "The bowlers didn't bowl the ball in the right areas," he said. "The ball was flying around everywhere. We're a better cricket team than that. We planned well, we just didn't execute anything that we wanted to do."

cards.headline: Canada earns first World Cup point with draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina
cards.teaser: Substitute Cyle Larin scored to give co-hosts Canada a 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina, securing the nation's first ever point at a World Cup.
cards.body:
Cyle Larin scored off the bench to equalize for Canada in a 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina, securing the nation's first-ever World Cup point. The result marks a historic moment as Canada competes as co-hosts in the tournament.

The draw reflects growing momentum around soccer in Canada, where the sport has surpassed hockey in youth participation. Coach Jesse Marsch noted the significant momentum building behind the team and the moment as the country looks to establish itself as a soccer nation.

cards.headline: Thomas Partey denied entry to Canada, misses Ghana World Cup opener
cards.teaser: Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey was refused entry to Canada and will miss his nation's first World Cup match against Panama in Toronto.
cards.body:
Thomas Partey has been denied entry to Canada and will miss Ghana's opening World Cup match against Panama in Toronto on Wednesday. The midfielder's visa application was refused by Canadian authorities.

The former Arsenal midfielder, now playing for Spanish club Villarreal, faces multiple rape charges in the UK. He was charged with five counts of rape and one count of sexual assault in July 2025, and received two additional rape charges in February. Partey has pleaded not guilty to all charges. FIFA confirmed the Canadian government made the entry decision.

cards.headline: Northampton defeats Leicester to reach Premiership final
cards.teaser: George Furbank scored two tries in his final home game as Northampton overcame Leicester in an East Midlands derby to secure a place in the Premiership final.
cards.body:
Northampton secured their place in the Premiership final with a 45-31 victory over Leicester in an thrilling East Midlands derby. Tom Litchfield was instrumental for the Saints, scoring a hat-trick in the first half to give Northampton a crucial advantage in a tightly contested match that swung back and forth throughout.

George Furbank added two tries in what proved to be an emotional final home appearance for the club. Archie McParland's try with 15 minutes remaining helped seal the victory. Northampton will face the winners of Bath versus Exeter in next week's final.

cards.headline: Kevin Sinfield knighted, six Lionesses receive MBEs
cards.teaser: Kevin Sinfield received a knighthood in the King's Birthday Honours while six members of England's Euro 2025-winning squad were made MBEs.
cards.body:
Kevin Sinfield has been knighted in the King's Birthday Honours, recognizing his outstanding fundraising work for motor neurone disease. The 45-year-old rugby league legend has raised more than £11 million in memory of Rob Burrow and becomes the second former rugby league player to receive a knighthood, following Billy Boston.

Six players from England's Euro 2025-winning women's football team have been made Members of the Order of the British Empire. Sinfield has pledged to continue his support for those living with motor neurone disease following the honor.

cards.headline: Phil Mickelson membership revoked amid inappropriate contact allegations
cards.teaser: Farms Golf Club in California revoked Phil Mickelson's membership following allegations of inappropriate contact with a female employee at the establishment.
cards.body:
Phil Mickelson's membership at The Farms golf club in San Diego has been terminated following allegations of inappropriate contact with a female employee. According to reports, the incident occurred before Mickelson played at the club in spring, with the employee accusing him of nonconsensual and inappropriate physical contact. Mickelson was confronted about the incident mid-round and subsequently left the property.

The club conducted an independent investigation that led to the membership revocation. A spokesperson for Mickelson stated that the matter has been resolved.

cards.headline: USA faces Paraguay in World Cup opener
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team prepares for its World Cup opening match against Paraguay in what observers call the biggest moment in the program's history.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team enters its World Cup opening match against Paraguay with high expectations as a co-host nation. Observers have characterized the moment as the biggest in the history of American men's soccer, with the team competing on home soil.

The match represents the start of a tournament that could define a generation of American players. As co-hosts, the pressure on the team to perform has intensified, with the home crowd expecting strong results. The game will be available for streaming, drawing significant interest from American soccer fans.

hero.headline: Gene Shalit, Today Show Film Critic for 40 Years, Dies at 100
hero.body:
Gene Shalit, the television personality known for his distinctive mustache and bow ties, died Friday at age 100. His family confirmed to NBC News that he "passed away peacefully today after 100 years of an amazing life."

Shalit became a recognizable fixture on NBC's Today Show, where he spent four decades reviewing films and books for morning television audiences. He appeared on the program from 1970 until his retirement in 2010, making him one of the longest-serving contributors in the show's history.

His signature appearance and playful approach to criticism helped bring film and book reviews to a mass audience at a time when such coverage was primarily found in newspapers and specialty publications. Shalit's accessible style and use of wordplay distinguished him from more serious critics of his era, and his reviews became known for their lighthearted tone and clever language.

During his 40-year tenure on Today, Shalit reviewed thousands of films and books, offering his perspectives on the latest cultural releases to millions of viewers each morning. His presence on the program made him one of the most recognizable television personalities of his generation. The combination of his distinctive look and his entertaining reviewing style earned him a dedicated following among the show's audience.

When Shalit retired in 2010 at age 84, his departure marked the end of a significant era in television criticism. For decades, his voice had been one of the most influential in shaping how American audiences thought about movies and literature. His ability to reach such a wide audience with his cultural commentary reflected a time when morning television could be a primary source of entertainment criticism for many viewers.

Shalit's career in broadcasting began in the early 1970s when he joined Today as a book and film reviewer. He gradually became a permanent fixture on the program, appearing regularly to share his thoughts on new releases. His approach to criticism emphasized accessibility and humor rather than academic analysis, making his reviews appealing to the general public.

His death marks the end of an important chapter in American television history. Shalit represented a generation of television personalities who could command large audiences and influence cultural conversations through their presence on morning news programs. His distinctive style and long-running role on Today helped establish the format for entertainment criticism on television, setting a template that would influence how movies and books were discussed on the medium for years to come.

NBC News confirmed his passing, with tributes from across the television industry noting his remarkable career and the lasting impact of his unique presence on American television.

cards.headline: Justice Department Approves Warner Bros Sale to Paramount for $111 Billion
cards.teaser: The Justice Department has approved Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros, clearing a major regulatory hurdle for the media merger.
cards.body:
The United States Justice Department has approved the $111 billion merger between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery. The deal, involving Paramount Skydance (controlled by the Ellison family) and Warner Bros Discovery, received clearance from the Justice Department's antitrust division following months of review.

The merger consolidates significant media assets, including CNN and HBO under Warner Bros Discovery, along with Paramount's CBS News. However, the deal faces additional scrutiny from UK regulators and could encounter legal challenges from state attorneys general. Industry observers have raised concerns that the merger will reduce competition in film studios and potentially harm the news sector by combining two major networks.

cards.headline: Chris Sanders to Direct Lilo & Stitch Live-Action Sequel
cards.teaser: The co-creator of the original Lilo & Stitch, who also voices the character Stitch, will direct the sequel to last year's live-action remake.
cards.body:
Chris Sanders, who co-created the original Lilo & Stitch animated film and voices Stitch, will direct the live-action sequel. Disney announced Sanders will take the helm of the follow-up after the studio's live-action remake became a major success.

Last year's live-action Lilo & Stitch remake delivered the biggest Memorial Day weekend opening in box office history and became Hollywood's first billion-dollar movie of the year. The financial performance prompted Disney to greenlight a sequel, bringing Sanders back to the franchise he helped create.

cards.headline: WABC News Anchor Bill Ritter Steps Down After Alzheimer's Diagnosis
cards.teaser: Bill Ritter announced his departure from the Eyewitness News anchor desk during his final broadcast, citing an early stage Alzheimer's diagnosis.
cards.body:
Bill Ritter has stepped down from his role as anchor of WABC-TV's Eyewitness News following an early stage Alzheimer's diagnosis. He announced his departure during Friday's 6 p.m. broadcast, his final newscast after more than two decades in the evening anchor chair.

Ritter joined the station's flagship broadcast in 2001 and has been a fixture at one of New York's most-watched local newscasts. He made the announcement after undergoing a series of medical tests that led to his diagnosis.

cards.headline: Washington National Opera Sues Kennedy Center for $17 Million in Donations
cards.teaser: The opera company filed suit to force the Kennedy Center to turn over $17 million in gifts it says are owed to the organization.
cards.body:
The Washington National Opera sued the Kennedy Center to recover $17 million in donations that the opera company says the center is withholding. The lawsuit seeks to force the Kennedy Center to turn over the funds that the opera company claims belong to it.

The legal action represents a significant dispute between the two Washington cultural institutions. The opera company alleges that the Kennedy Center owes it the money from donations that were intended for the opera's use.

cards.headline: Directors Guild Limits TV Actors From Directing Episodes
cards.teaser: The DGA secured a contract provision restricting actors on TV series from directing episodes, aiming to preserve jobs for career directors.
cards.body:
The Directors Guild of America secured a provision in its new contract that limits actors on television series from directing episodes. The move aims to preserve directing jobs for career television directors amid a prolonged production downturn.

The provision addresses a 40 percent decline in production jobs over the last four years, which has affected employment opportunities for directors. The guild negotiated the restriction as part of efforts to protect work for its members during the industry slowdown.

cards.headline: Viral YouTube Short 'Open Door' Gets Six-Figure Film Deal
cards.teaser: A sci-fi short film with nearly 15 million views across platforms will be adapted into a feature through a six-figure development deal.
cards.body:
Open Door, a viral sci-fi short by Kevin Cates with nearly 15 million views across YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram, will be adapted into a feature-length film. The project secured a six-figure development deal, continuing a trend of studios investing in content from YouTube creators.

The deal follows the success of horror films Obsession and Backrooms, as the entertainment industry increasingly looks to YouTube creators and younger filmmakers with established audiences. Cates' short attracted significant online viewership before catching the attention of film studios.

hero.headline: Census Bureau may limit public data under Trump privacy policy
hero.teaser: The Trump administration is pushing to reduce what it calls statistical noise in Census Bureau data, a move that could limit the amount of public information available for redistricting and other uses.
hero.body:
The Trump administration is moving to limit the ways the Census Bureau can protect privacy when releasing statistics, a change that officials say will cut statistical noise from the data. The policy shift could result in less public data being available from the bureau.

The change would affect new public data used for redistricting and other purposes. Trump officials are directing the bureau to alter its privacy protection methods, which could reduce the amount of detailed statistical information released to the public.

cards.headline: US and Iran near agreement on nuclear deal, senior official says
cards.teaser: The United States is close to finalizing an agreement with Iran, with a senior US official estimating an 80 to 85 percent chance of success in the near term.
cards.body:
President Trump announced he is canceling planned missile strikes on Iran, saying a peace deal is near. A senior US official estimates an 80 to 85 percent chance of success for a near-term agreement, though nuclear details will take months to finalize.

Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday that he expected to sign a deal with Iran within days. However, Iran's foreign ministry has not confirmed that a final decision on an agreement has been reached, dismissing Trump's claims about the timeline.

cards.headline: Democrat calls for Vance, White House officials to testify on Epstein files
cards.teaser: A top House Oversight Committee Democrat has asked Chairman James Comer to call Vice President Vance and other Trump administration officials for testimony following a report about White House efforts related to Jeffrey Epstein files.
cards.body:
Representative Robert Garcia pressed Chairman James Comer in a letter on Friday to take immediate steps to call several Trump administration officials for questioning. The request follows a report on the White House's alleged efforts to contain a scandal surrounding convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Garcia, a top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, urged Comer to summon Vice President Vance and other White House officials for testimony. The letter asks the committee to investigate the administration's handling of files and information related to Epstein's crimes.

cards.headline: ICE detention numbers drop despite expanded bed capacity
cards.teaser: Immigration and Customs Enforcement has empty detention bed space with the average daily number of detainees falling to 58,000, despite a $38 billion expansion effort.
cards.body:
ICE has empty detention bed space and the average daily number of detainees has fallen to 58,000, according to two sources familiar with the data. The agency went on a $38 billion buying spree to rapidly expand the number of available beds during Trump's presidency.

After the detention population more than doubled in President Trump's first year in office, the numbers have since declined. Trump backed off aggressive city-wide enforcement strategies following the killing of two US citizens in Minneapolis, leading to the drop in detention population.

cards.headline: Justice Department clears Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros.
cards.teaser: The Department of Justice has approved Paramount's $110 billion bid to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing a regulatory hurdle for the merger between the entertainment companies.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has approved Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, clearing a major regulatory hurdle for the merger. The antitrust division's decision allows the two entertainment giants to move forward with combining their operations.

However, the deal faces additional scrutiny. The merger is still under investigation in the UK and could face legal challenges from state attorneys general. Industry observers have raised concerns that combining the companies could reduce competition in the film studio market and result in the consolidation of news operations, particularly CBS News and CNN.

cards.headline: Comer requests Alan Dershowitz testimony in Epstein probe
cards.teaser: House Oversight Chairman James Comer has formally requested that lawyer Alan Dershowitz testify before the committee as part of its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's crimes.
cards.body:
Representative James Comer has formally requested that lawyer Alan Dershowitz testify before the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee regarding its investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's crimes. Comer's request is based on public reporting, Department of Justice documents, materials obtained by the committee, and Dershowitz's former involvement with the case.

The request comes as the committee continues examining Epstein's criminal activities and the individuals connected to him.

cards.headline: Google sues Chinese cybercrime network over AI misuse
cards.teaser: Google filed a lawsuit against a Chinese cybercrime network, alleging the hackers used the company's Gemini AI models to build phishing software designed to rob consumers.
cards.body:
Google filed a lawsuit Friday in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York against a Chinese cybercrime group called "Outsider Enterprise." The operation allegedly used Google's Gemini AI models to create phishing software designed to defraud consumers.

According to Google's claims, the cybercrime network used the company's AI technology to develop phishing tools and launched a massive scam campaign. The group sent 2.5 million text messages over two weeks, targeting hundreds of thousands of victims with fraudulent schemes.
